name: s4_recon_keeps
title: Reconstructors rebuild position from real text but not from a sentence that states it
caption: Exp 14, 200 items per row. A: a probe trained on Oracle Lens's reconstructor output for the true 32-token span (grouped 5-fold) separates every row; fed Oracle Lens's own bullets it falls to 0.54-0.66 on the position rows but not on language. Right: a one-sentence statement moves each reconstructor's output along the true class direction by under 0.30 of the gap on every position row; only the language statement through the NLA's critic clears it (0.72). Statements are the fixed labels, e.g. 'The text is in French' (NLA critic) and '- French language' (Oracle Lens). Oracle Lens's reconstructor ignores even '- French language' (0.10); its 1.39 comes from a bullet written in French. Caveat: aggregates only (no per-item file is local), so no intervals; Oracle Lens reconstructor at layer 44, in its whitened output space.

notes: Statements: NLA critic uses the fixed-label sentence of the NLA ('The current cell is in the first/fifth column of the table', 'The current position is inside/outside a parenthesis', 'This is item number two/nine in the list', 'The text is in French/German'); Oracle Lens's reconstructor uses its fixed bullet ('- column one/five', '- inside/outside parentheses', '- item two/nine', '- French/German language'). As a share of the class gap, Oracle Lens bullets keep table column 0.12, inside parentheses 0.18, list item index 0.07, ij2_lang 0.28. The talk table mixes units (span and bullets rows are probe AUROCs, the statement row a gap share) and pairs a descriptive statement for position with an exhibiting French bullet for language. No raw per-item reconstructions are on disk; numbers are read from the analysis14_*.json aggregates.
